B.1 Proof of Lemma 1

We first restate the lemma and then prove it.

Lemma 5.

Let ℛ\mathcal{R} satisfy the symmetry conditions above, and let s≤r≤ns\leq r\leq n. Fix 𝐲∈ℝn{\mathbf{y}}\in\mathbb{R}^{n} and λ>0\lambda>0.

If dom⁡(ℛ)⊆ℝ+n\mathop{\mbox{\rm dom}}(\mathcal{R})\subseteq\mathbb{R}_{+}^{n}, let TT contain the indices of the rr largest entries of 𝐲{\mathbf{y}}. If ℛ\mathcal{R} is invariant under coordinate-wise sign changes, let TT contain the indices of the rr largest entries of 𝐲{\mathbf{y}} in absolute value. Let

𝐮^∈argmin𝐮∈ℝr{λ​‖𝐮−𝐲T‖2+ℛ⁡(𝐈T​𝐮)},𝐱^:=𝐈T​𝐮^.\widehat{{\mathbf{u}}}\in\argmin_{{\mathbf{u}}\in\mathbb{R}^{r}}\left\{\lambda\left\lVert{\mathbf{u}}-{\mathbf{y}}_{T}\right\rVert^{2}+\mathcal{R}({\mathbf{I}}_{T}{\mathbf{u}})\right\},\qquad\widehat{{\mathbf{x}}}:={\mathbf{I}}_{T}\widehat{{\mathbf{u}}}.

Then

𝐱^∈argmin𝐱∈𝒞r{λ​‖𝐱−𝐲‖2+ℛ⁡(𝐱)}.\widehat{{\mathbf{x}}}\in\argmin_{{\mathbf{x}}\in\mathcal{C}_{r}}\left\{\lambda\left\lVert{\mathbf{x}}-{\mathbf{y}}\right\rVert^{2}+\mathcal{R}({\mathbf{x}})\right\}.

Consequently, if every 𝐱∗∈𝒳∗{\mathbf{x}}^{*}\in\mathcal{X}^{*} is ss-sparse, then for every r≥sr\geq s this construction implements a weak proximal oracle.

Proof.

Fix any 𝐳∈𝒞r{\mathbf{z}}\in\mathcal{C}_{r}. Consider first the case dom⁡(ℛ)⊆ℝ+n\mathop{\mbox{\rm dom}}(\mathcal{R})\subseteq\mathbb{R}_{+}^{n}. By permuting the coordinates of 𝐳{\mathbf{z}}, we may place its nonzero entries on the coordinates in TT, pairing its largest entries with the largest entries of 𝐲{\mathbf{y}}. Denote the resulting point by 𝐳~\widetilde{{\mathbf{z}}}. By permutation invariance, ℛ⁡(𝐳~)=ℛ⁡(𝐳)\mathcal{R}(\widetilde{{\mathbf{z}}})=\mathcal{R}({\mathbf{z}}), ‖𝐳~‖=‖𝐳‖\left\lVert\widetilde{{\mathbf{z}}}\right\rVert=\left\lVert{\mathbf{z}}\right\rVert. Moreover, the rearrangement inequality gives ⟨𝐳~,𝐲⟩≥⟨𝐳,𝐲⟩\left\langle\widetilde{{\mathbf{z}}},{\mathbf{y}}\right\rangle\geq\left\langle{\mathbf{z}},{\mathbf{y}}\right\rangle. Hence,

λ​‖𝐳~−𝐲‖2+ℛ⁡(𝐳~)≤λ​‖𝐳−𝐲‖2+ℛ⁡(𝐳).\lambda\left\lVert\widetilde{{\mathbf{z}}}-{\mathbf{y}}\right\rVert^{2}+\mathcal{R}(\widetilde{{\mathbf{z}}})\leq\lambda\left\lVert{\mathbf{z}}-{\mathbf{y}}\right\rVert^{2}+\mathcal{R}({\mathbf{z}}).

If ℛ\mathcal{R} is invariant under coordinate-wise sign changes, first change the signs of the nonzero entries of 𝐳{\mathbf{z}} to agree with the corresponding signs of 𝐲{\mathbf{y}}, and then permute their absolute values so that the largest ones are paired with the rr largest entries of 𝐲{\mathbf{y}} in absolute value. Signed permutation invariance again preserves both ℛ⁡(𝐳)\mathcal{R}({\mathbf{z}}) and ‖𝐳‖\left\lVert{\mathbf{z}}\right\rVert, while the inner product with 𝐲{\mathbf{y}} cannot decrease. The same inequality therefore holds.

Thus, in either case, for every 𝐳∈𝒞r{\mathbf{z}}\in\mathcal{C}_{r} there is a point with support contained in TT whose proximal objective is no larger. It remains only to minimize over points supported on TT. For 𝐱=𝐈T​𝐮{\mathbf{x}}={\mathbf{I}}_{T}{\mathbf{u}},

‖𝐱−𝐲‖2=‖𝐮−𝐲T‖2+‖𝐲Tc‖2,\left\lVert{\mathbf{x}}-{\mathbf{y}}\right\rVert^{2}=\left\lVert{\mathbf{u}}-{\mathbf{y}}_{T}\right\rVert^{2}+\left\lVert{\mathbf{y}}_{T^{c}}\right\rVert^{2},

where the second term is independent of 𝐮{\mathbf{u}}. Hence the minimizer is precisely 𝐱^=𝐈T​𝐮^\widehat{{\mathbf{x}}}={\mathbf{I}}_{T}\widehat{{\mathbf{u}}} defined above.

Finally, since r≥sr\geq s, every 𝐱∗∈𝒳∗{\mathbf{x}}^{*}\in\mathcal{X}^{*} belongs to 𝒞r\mathcal{C}_{r}. Therefore, we indeed have that for every 𝐱∗∈𝒳∗{\mathbf{x}}^{*}\in\mathcal{X}^{*},

λ​‖𝐱^−𝐲‖2+ℛ⁡(𝐱^)≤λ​‖𝐱∗−𝐲‖2+ℛ⁡(𝐱∗).\lambda\left\lVert\widehat{{\mathbf{x}}}-{\mathbf{y}}\right\rVert^{2}+\mathcal{R}(\widehat{{\mathbf{x}}})\leq\lambda\left\lVert{\mathbf{x}}^{*}-{\mathbf{y}}\right\rVert^{2}+\mathcal{R}({\mathbf{x}}^{*}).

and

∥𝐔rDiag(𝐮)𝐕r⊤−𝐘∥F2=‖𝐮−𝝈1:r‖2+∑i=r+1qσi2.\|{{\mathbf{U}}_{r}\operatorname{Diag}({\mathbf{u}}){\mathbf{V}}_{r}^{\top}-{\mathbf{Y}}}\|_{F}^{2}=\left\lVert{\mathbf{u}}-\boldsymbol{\sigma}_{1:r}\right\rVert^{2}+\sum_{i=r+1}^{q}\sigma_{i}^{2}.

Since dom⁡(ℛ)⊆𝕊+d\mathop{\mbox{\rm dom}}(\mathcal{R})\subseteq\mathbb{S}_{+}^{d}, the matrix 𝐗{\mathbf{X}} is positive semidefinite. The matrices 𝐗{\mathbf{X}} and 𝐗~\widetilde{{\mathbf{X}}} have the same eigenvalues, and therefore ℛ⁡(𝐗~)=ℛ⁡(𝐗)\mathcal{R}(\widetilde{{\mathbf{X}}})=\mathcal{R}({\mathbf{X}}). The trace inequality for symmetric matrices gives ⟨𝐗,𝐘⟩≤∑i=1rτi​γi=⟨𝐗~,𝐘⟩\langle{{\mathbf{X}},{\mathbf{Y}}}\rangle\leq\sum_{i=1}^{r}\tau_{i}\gamma_{i}=\langle{\widetilde{{\mathbf{X}}},{\mathbf{Y}}}\rangle. Since 𝐗{\mathbf{X}} and 𝐗~\widetilde{{\mathbf{X}}} also have the same Frobenius norm, ‖𝐗~−𝐘‖F2≤‖𝐗−𝐘‖F2\|{\widetilde{{\mathbf{X}}}-{\mathbf{Y}}}\|_{F}^{2}\leq\|{{\mathbf{X}}-{\mathbf{Y}}}\|_{F}^{2}. Thus, every rank-rr candidate can be replaced, without increasing the proximal objective, by one whose eigenvectors agree with the leading eigenvectors of 𝐘{\mathbf{Y}} and whose nonzero eigenvalues are nonincreasing.

As above, the ordering constraint is redundant. For any 𝐮∈ℝ+r{\mathbf{u}}\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{r}, permutation invariance of ρ\rho and the rearrangement inequality give ρ⁡((𝐮↓,𝟎d−r))=ρ⁡((𝐮,𝟎d−r))\rho\!\left(({\mathbf{u}}^{\downarrow},\mathbf{0}_{d-r})\right)=\rho\!\left(({\mathbf{u}},\mathbf{0}_{d-r})\right) and ‖𝐮↓−𝜸1:r‖2≤‖𝐮−𝜸1:r‖2\left\lVert{\mathbf{u}}^{\downarrow}-\boldsymbol{\gamma}_{1:r}\right\rVert^{2}\leq\left\lVert{\mathbf{u}}-\boldsymbol{\gamma}_{1:r}\right\rVert^{2}. Moreover,

ℛ⁡(𝐔r​Diag⁡(𝐮)​𝐔r⊤)=ρ⁡((𝐮,𝟎d−r))\mathcal{R}\!\left({\mathbf{U}}_{r}\operatorname{Diag}({\mathbf{u}}){\mathbf{U}}_{r}^{\top}\right)=\rho\!\left(({\mathbf{u}},\mathbf{0}_{d-r})\right)

and

∥𝐔rDiag(𝐮)𝐔r⊤−𝐘∥F2=‖𝐮−𝜸1:r‖2+∑i=r+1dγi2.\|{{\mathbf{U}}_{r}\operatorname{Diag}({\mathbf{u}}){\mathbf{U}}_{r}^{\top}-{\mathbf{Y}}}\|_{F}^{2}=\left\lVert{\mathbf{u}}-\boldsymbol{\gamma}_{1:r}\right\rVert^{2}+\sum_{i=r+1}^{d}\gamma_{i}^{2}.

The last sum is independent of 𝐮{\mathbf{u}}. Hence, the scalar problem defining 𝐮^\widehat{{\mathbf{u}}} is exactly the remaining part of the rank-rr proximal problem, and 𝐗^\widehat{{\mathbf{X}}} is again a minimizer.

Finally, if every 𝐗∗∈𝒳∗{\mathbf{X}}^{*}\in\mathcal{X}^{*} has rank at most rr, then 𝐗∗∈𝒞r{\mathbf{X}}^{*}\in\mathcal{C}_{r}, and therefore, in either setting,

λ​‖𝐗^−𝐘‖F2+ℛ⁡(𝐗^)≤λ​‖𝐗∗−𝐘‖F2+ℛ⁡(𝐗∗).\lambda\|{\widehat{{\mathbf{X}}}-{\mathbf{Y}}}\|_{F}^{2}+\mathcal{R}(\widehat{{\mathbf{X}}})\leq\lambda\|{{\mathbf{X}}^{*}-{\mathbf{Y}}}\|_{F}^{2}+\mathcal{R}({\mathbf{X}}^{*}).
